clue.text: Prepare to take off burden placed on one

parts.note: a tax is a burden or strain
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone shoulders a heavy load before a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft rolls along the runway on its wheels before it takes off; that movement is its own verb.

clue.text: Supporting male that's upset, in difficult situation

indicators.note: one piece placed in another means it sits inside the word for a difficult situation

parts.note: to be in a bind is to be in a tight spot

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so the word for a male is read the other way round

parts.note: the pronoun for a male, written backwards

explanation.surface: An upset man in a tight spot needs someone supporting him.
explanation.definitionFit: To be behind someone is to back them, as with a cause or a candidate.

clue.text: Part of mathematical solution in addition

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, so the answer lies inside them

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sum's answer comes with an addition step.
explanation.walkthrough: The maths words suggest arithmetic, but they only house the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is a plain synonym meaning as well or besides.

clue.text: Mounted like fish or reptile

definitions.meaning: first meaning: climbed up, as a wall or a peak
second meaning: covered in small overlapping plates of skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a stuffed specimen mounted for display; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both climbed and having a skin of horny plates, as fish and snakes do.

clue.text: Date and hour arranged, as written

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two words of fodder

explanation.surface: A meeting time is fixed in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a book is to write it, so the past participle is a synonym of written.

clue.text: Record I had accomplished hard to beat

parts.note: form is a record of past performance, or in British slang a criminal record
the contraction I'd
able means skilled or competent

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their record achievement will be tough to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A formidable opponent inspires fear or respect because they are so strong.

clue.text: Vessel held back in middle of trip for so long

indicators.note: placed in the middle of a word means it goes inside it

parts.note: to trip is to stumble or fall

indicators.note: held back suggests drawn backwards, so the vessel's name runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug, written backwards here

explanation.surface: A boat stays behind partway through a voyage for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'trip' suggest a sea voyage, but the vessel is a jug and the trip a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is a casual way of saying goodbye, the same parting word.

clue.text: Like many pots holding a little corn at that point

parts.note: an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant, a small part of a crop
then means at that time

explanation.surface: Pots storing grain at a particular moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots are commonly made of baked clay, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Company at the point of producing voucher

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for company
upon can mean at the moment of, as in 'upon arrival'

explanation.surface: A firm is about to issue a voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a ticket or slip giving a discount, so it is a kind of voucher.

clue.text: End of road more affected by freeze, hence more dangerous

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word road
comparative of icy

explanation.surface: The far stretch of a road ices over worse, so it is riskier.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicey is informal for risky or hazardous, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Authorise priest seizing house in this state

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it

indicators.note: something seizing another grabs and holds it, so the abbreviation for house goes within

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A priest's licence to take over a property in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is one of the fifty United States, in the south-central region.

clue.text: Common complaint taken on as responsibility not warmly embraced

parts.note: the common cold is a widespread ailment
to shoulder a burden is to accept it

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with an everyday ailment as their duty gets no warm welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them, the idiom here as a hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Knowing all income isn't redistributed

indicators.note: anything redistributed is shared out afresh, so the letters are dealt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A know-all claims earnings are not shared out more fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Latin for all-knowing, describes having unlimited knowledge.

clue.text: Take strength from male soldier in international force?

parts.note: the United Nations, whose peacekeepers are an international force
a man is both a male and a private soldier

explanation.surface: Asks whether a male soldier serving with the UN might lose his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the soldier in the force is read as UN plus man, rather than one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to deprive them of courage or self-control.

clue.text: Was familiar with central character in Dickens novel

indicators.note: the central character of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: A reader knew the main figure in a book by Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central character' and 'novel' point to fiction, but one is a middle letter and the other an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew, the past tense of know, means had acquaintance with or understood.

clue.text: Singer finding warmth in clothing

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: wear is clothing, as in menswear
a synonym of warmth

explanation.surface: A vocalist gets warm in stage costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird, so it is a singer in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Person wandering, in their right mind? On the contrary

parts.note: read as 'no' to the next word
the contrary of being in one's right mind is being insane

explanation.surface: Asks whether a drifter is sane, then answers that they are not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words meaning 'not insane'; the question then flips it, since a wanderer's mind is the opposite of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Spirited sprinting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lively and stylish, as a hero

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a lively runner; the words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stylishly bold and, as a participle, rushing at speed.

clue.text: Non-U first performance that's outstanding

definitions.note: a phrase for a thing still owed, standing for the noun

indicators.note: non- means without, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance on stage
the letter itself, also the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A down-market opening night that proves a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the old British label for language thought lower-class, but here it simply removes U.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owing, and unpaid sums are said to be outstanding.

clue.text: Tailor still reserving expensive shiny material

indicators.note: to tailor something is to cut and reshape it, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor holds back a pricey glossy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserving' looks like a container signal, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling silver is a valuable alloy of 92.5 percent silver, prized for its lustre.

clue.text: How some German music sounds for important member of orchestra

indicators.note: how something sounds refers to pronunciation, so the answer is spoken like the German music

parts.note: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: Describes the sound of German songs played by an orchestra's top player.
explanation.definitionFit: In British orchestras the leader is the principal first violinist, second only to the conductor.

clue.text: Caption, for example, needed in advance

indicators.note: something needed in another goes inside it

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A caption such as one must be prepared beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the wording beneath a picture or map, explaining it.

clue.text: Subject to diversion as one's entering key area

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

parts.note: D is a musical key
one's read as one is, I being one
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: A traffic diversion is imposed as a vehicle enters a main zone.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract someone is to divert their attention elsewhere.

clue.text: City impacted by long-term investment effort? Nothing in it

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A financial question about a long-term investment that gives no return.
explanation.walkthrough: Investment is the old military word for a siege; the Greeks besieged this city for ten years.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy endured a ten-year siege in Greek legend, a long investment in the military sense.

clue.text: Producer of old pictures, some requiring restoration

indicators.note: some of the following words means just a portion of their letters is used

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some old paintings need conservation work.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a nineteenth-century French painter, so a maker of old pictures.

clue.text: Player in deal, as featured in very successful movie

indicators.note: something featured in another appears within it

parts.note: E.T., Spielberg's hugely successful 1982 film
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor signs a deal to appear in a blockbuster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'deal' suggest a film contract, but the deal is of cards at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and cards are dealt to each.

clue.text: Pay to serve and start fighting

definitions.meaning: second meaning: join battle with an enemy

explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joins two separate meanings, though the surface suggests hiring soldiers who then go to war.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to employ someone and to enter combat with an opponent.

clue.text: Keyboard player in trio sang poorly

indicators.note: something done poorly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keyboard player in a vocal group sang badly.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist plays the organ, an instrument with one or more keyboards.
